_comment: Registry for the Finance department. Holds the fiscal calendar, the business-line definitions, the project-sale exclusion rule, the variance vocabulary and the alert thresholds. Consumed by scripts/finance_reconcile.py, .claude/commands/finance-close.md and (from Phase 5) .claude/agents/qbo-actions-agent.md. Method: methods/finance-reconciliation.md. Output contract: contracts/finance-period-schema.md. QBO connection config lives separately in platform-settings/quickbooks.json; Lightspeed API config in platform-settings/lightspeed.json.
_maintenance: EVERY id in this file marked `null` with an `_unverified` note is a rule that MATCHES NOTHING until it is filled in. That failure is SILENT and it inflates the number it was meant to exclude — the same class of failure as the catalogue routine's `Extraction Status` filter on 2026-09-10, which matched zero rows without erroring. scripts/finance_reconcile.py MUST refuse to run while a required id is null rather than produce a plausible wrong answer. Re-verify against live data whenever a match count drops to zero unexpectedly.

fiscal_calendar._comment: Titan's corporate year ends September 30. Months are the atom; quarters are derived, never stored. Fiscal is the default spine for anything that rolls up (YTD, quarters, bonus pools); calendar is carried so a renderer can offer that view without recomputing it.
fiscal_calendar._fiscal_year_rule: A period belongs to the fiscal year whose September 30 year end it falls before or on. 2026-08 is FY2026; 2026-10 is FY2027.
fiscal_calendar._never_print_bare_quarter: "Q1" means Oct-Dec fiscally and Jan-Mar calendrically — a quarter apart. Every rendered label carries both the fiscal year and the month range: `FY26 Q2 (Jan-Mar)`. This is a hard rule for every consumer, not a style preference.

business_lines._comment: Each line names the ONE system authoritative for it (methods/finance-reconciliation.md, authority table). `basis` is copied onto every figure in the period file so two lines computed from different systems never look alike on a dashboard without saying so.

project._margin_note: Margin comes from Notion's own rollups (Total Flooring Material Cost / Revenue / Profit, Total Labor Cost, Total Other Costs). It is NEVER computed from Lightspeed — LS books project sales at cost = revenue, so LS reports zero margin on them by construction.

store._exclusion_note: Project sales are removed by project_sale_identification below before this line's margin is computed.

other._comment: Income that reaches QBO through neither Lightspeed nor a Notion project — e.g. delivery-only charges billed directly, rebates, interest. Defined by exclusion, so it is the line to watch when a figure looks wrong.

business_lines._never_summed: Lines render side by side. company{} in the period file is computed independently from company-level revenue and cost, NEVER by summing or averaging these. Same refusal as project vs STORE pipeline value.

project_sale_identification._comment: How a Lightspeed sale is recognised as a project sale, so it can be excluded from store gross margin and attributed to its project instead.
project_sale_identification._verified_2026_09_11: Established by a full walk of all 55,820 Lightspeed sales. This REPLACES the earlier 'Poreus account' hypothesis, which did not survive contact with the data — see _poreus_finding.

join_key.resolves_to: Notion Titan Projects `userDefined:ID` (auto_increment), mirrored as `Project ID` on the Airtable Project Log table.
join_key._confirmed_overlap: PP-447 and PP-449 appear both in Lightspeed sale notes and in Airtable Project Log rows. The join is real and it works.

project_sale_identification._coverage_warning: ONLY 20 SALES IN THE ENTIRE 55,820-SALE HISTORY CARRY A PP-### NOTE, 19 distinct projects, and EVERY ONE IS DATED 2026 — almost all on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10. This convention is about two days old. It is the right join key going forward; it attributes essentially NO historical project revenue. Any backfill before 2026-09-09 needs a different method, or an accepted gap.
project_sale_identification._poreus_finding: Albert described project sales being rung 'under the Poreus account'. No Lightspeed CUSTOMER named Poreus/Porous exists — all 2,779 customers were scanned. There IS a Lightspeed USER 'Pourya' (57c18364-4307-455f-8942-f18f61e4b555, cashier, pourya@titanfloors.ca), who is also the `Sales Person` on the Airtable project rows, so 'Poreus' is very likely 'Pourya'. BUT Pourya has rung only 2 sales in all of Lightspeed history, one of them on 2026-09-10. So user_id is NOT a usable project-sale marker today. ASK ALBERT what 'the Poreus account' refers to before encoding anything here.

user_account.name: Pourya
user_account._why_not: 2 sales in 55,820. Using it as an identifying signal would match essentially nothing, and a rule that matches nothing fails silently.

project_sale_identification.observed_statuses_on_project_sales: Of the 12 most recent PP-tagged sales: 4 ONACCOUNT, 2 LAYBY_CLOSED, 1 LAYBY, 4 CLOSED, 1 SAVED. Project sales sit squarely in the layaway and on-account gaps — they are not an edge case in this reconciliation, they are most of it.
project_sale_identification._zero_value_sales: PP-416 carries total_price_incl 0.00. Zero-value sales exist and must not be assumed to be errors — check whether they are pack/fulfilment records before treating them as revenue or as bugs.
project_sale_identification._unmatched_note: An LS sale carrying a PP-### that matches no project is unattributed revenue: it goes to needs_attention, is never dropped, and is never silently left in the store line.

variance_types._comment: Closed vocabulary. Adding a value is an edit to this file, methods/finance-reconciliation.md AND contracts/finance-period-schema.md in the same change. `expected: false` types always produce a needs_attention entry — they mean something is wrong, as opposed to the system working as designed.

layaway_deposit.description: Cash taken on a layaway not yet redeemed. Never synced to QBO. A liability, not revenue.

layaway_redemption.description: Layaway closed, goods released. Revenue is recognised here, not at deposit.

on_account_charge.description: AR created in Lightspeed; may or may not have reached QBO.

on_account_edit_drift.description: LS and QBO both hold the sale and disagree. An LS edit never propagates to the QBO mirror, so nothing else will ever surface this.

external_project_payment.description: Project money that reached the bank without an LS sale — paid cash or externally.

unexplained.description: Residual after every other type is applied. Reported, never absorbed.

authority._comment: Which system wins when two disagree. There is no midpoint and no average — the loser is corrected, not blended. Mirrors the table in methods/finance-reconciliation.md.
authority._ar_note: LS wins because an EDIT to an on-account sale never reaches QBO. The QBO figure will look plausible forever, which is exactly why it cannot be trusted as a second opinion.
authority._payments_note: A Notion payments-log figure is money received, NOT bookkeeping. departments.json already records it as a partial-answer source; that label must survive into every downstream render.

thresholds._comment: What lands in needs_attention. Money in integer cents CAD.
thresholds._coverage_floor_note: Below this, the period's headline figures are rendered with an explicit low-confidence marker. The floor is a RENDERING threshold, never a gate that reclassifies residuals to clear it — coverage is a measurement, not a target.
thresholds._margin_floor_note: A completed project below this margin is surfaced for review. It is not an error — some jobs are deliberately thin — but it is always worth a look.

opex_allocation._comment: Operating expenses are NOT allocated across business lines. Splitting shared overhead needs an arbitrary basis, and publishing the result as 'project net profit' would be false precision — a number that looks authoritative and is not.
opex_allocation._if_ever_enabled: Requires a stated basis (e.g. revenue_share) AND a visible `allocated: true` flag on every figure derived from it. Never a silent default.

paths._namespace_note: Approvals live under finance/, not plans/<date>/, because a period is not a day. plans/ is a day-scoped namespace and forcing a month into it would make the prefix-matching rule in contracts/dept-plan-schema.md ambiguous.

project_financials_source._comment: Where the computed project P&L is actually readable. This is the single most important constraint in the whole pipeline.
project_financials_source._blocker: NOTION MONEY VALUES CANNOT BE READ VIA MCP. Every money property on Project Financials is a formula or rollup, and the Notion MCP returns those as opaque formulaResult:// / rollupResult:// URIs rather than numbers. Verified 2026-09-11 on a live page. The `financials-relation-sync` skill documents the same behaviour as '<omitted />'. Reading Project Financials directly is therefore NOT a viable path, and the plan that assumed it was is wrong.

primary._why: A flattened, machine-readable mirror of the same 416 Notion Project Financials rows, carrying real numbers where Notion carries formulas: Revenue, Total Project Profit, Overall Margin, Profit (Store Calcs), Labor Cost, NFM Cost, Other Costs, Flooring Material Revenue, Flooring Material Cost, Total Sqft Sold, and Project ID as PP-###.
primary._unknown: HOW Project Log is kept in sync with Notion was NOT established. No Make scenario named for it was found. If it is a manual export, its freshness is a standing risk and the period file must carry the mirror's own as-of date, not the run date.

fallback._comment: Raw inputs that ARE readable from Notion, to recompute from if the Airtable mirror goes stale.
fallback.flooring_line_items: collection://a84d8ff8-32c5-4174-b00c-ace45222f7cc — Sqft Sold, Cost Rate, Sold At Rate are plain numbers (254/275 populated).
fallback.project_costs: collection://304596a4-505f-8197-b065-000bddcd731a — Cost is a plain number, precision 0 (1031/1045 populated). Category: Labor / Materials (Non-Flooring) / Disposal / Delivery / Other.
fallback.titan_projects: collection://1b4596a4-505f-81ca-b1d5-000bb73ecbe1 — Value Approx is a plain number (431/436).

notion_project_financials._role: Authoritative for the DEFINITIONS (its formulas are the company's margin logic) but not machine-readable for VALUES. Read the formula descriptions here; read the numbers from Airtable.

data_quality_findings._comment: Measured 2026-09-11. Each is a real limit on what the period file can claim, and each belongs in needs_attention rather than being quietly absorbed.
data_quality_findings.unlinked_payments: 81 of 562 Master Payments Log rows (14%) have no project relation. That money is received but unattributable.
data_quality_findings.no_expense_data_since_2025_01: The Airtable Expense Entries table (3,843 rows) stops at 2025-01-01. Both Monthly Expenses rollup tables are empty shells of zeros created in one batch on 2026-01-19 — which is why the old Airtable 'Total Net Profit' equals gross profit exactly. Operating expenses must come from QBO; there is no other source.
data_quality_findings.abandoned_airtable_rollups: Monthly Rollup (89 rows) and its KPI/metrics stack stop at 2025-09-30. POS Flooring Data (Quarterly) stops at Q2 2025. Monthly Financial Performance Summary was designed and never populated. These are the manual consolidation this pipeline replaces — useful as a reference for WHAT was measured, not as a data source.
data_quality_findings.checkbox_signal_loss: Costs Complete and Commission Paid Out are __YES__ on all 416 Project Financials rows. They carry no discriminating power and must not be used as filters.
data_quality_findings.relation_asymmetry: Financials -> Flooring Line Items is 58% populated; the reverse relation on line items is 8%. The financials-relation-sync skill patches this MANUALLY, as a snapshot. Treat the reverse relation as unreliable.
data_quality_findings.missing_costs: Project Costs contains explicit gap markers such as 'Labor Missing For 616' with a null Cost. A null cost is an UNKNOWN margin, never a high one — see data_quality[] in contracts/finance-period-schema.md.
data_quality_findings.undocumented_select_field: Master Payments Log has a `Select` field (TA/B/T/S/R/SC/C) populated on every sampled row with no recorded meaning. Ask before using it for anything.
data_quality_findings.not_in_notion: There is NO invoices, expenses, purchase-order, supplier-bill, quote, deposit, or chart-of-accounts database in Notion. Do not assume one exists.
